name: Menefee 2011 (OARS)
question: Does freehand porcine-dermis graft or polypropylene-mesh paravaginal repair reduce anterior prolapse failure compared with anterior colporrhaphy?

design.population: Ninety-nine women with symptomatic stage II or greater anterior vaginal wall prolapse who desired surgery were randomized at two centers.
design.description: Two-center, blinded, three-arm superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Publisher full text, Materials and Methods; Results, first paragraph

verdictNote: Anatomic benefit did not produce a significant difference in composite failure.
takeaway: At two years, freehand polypropylene-mesh vaginal paravaginal repair had less stage II-or-greater anterior prolapse than porcine-dermis graft repair or anterior colporrhaphy; composite failure did not differ significantly among groups.

reports.label: Two-year primary report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation and Crossref published-print field give December 2011 without a day
reports.citation: Menefee SA, Dyer KY, Lukacz ES, Simsiman AJ, Luber KM, Nguyen JN. "Colporrhaphy Compared With Mesh or Graft-Reinforced Vaginal Paravaginal Repair for Anterior Vaginal Wall Prolapse: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;118(6):1337-1344. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e318237edc4
reports.followUpLocator: Publisher full text, Results, first paragraph

results.measure: Stage II-or-greater anterior prolapse at minimum 2 years
results.note: Failure meant Ba at -1 cm or greater. Mesh versus porcine graft P=0.015; graft versus colporrhaphy P=0.430. Prespecified two-sided alpha was 5%; planned 33 participants per arm for a 40-percentage-point anatomic-success difference.
results.locator: Publisher full text, Materials and Methods, power-analysis paragraph; Results, paragraph beginning 'The anatomic failure rate'

results.measure: Intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis with missing data designated failures
results.note: All missing outcomes counted as failures.
results.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'The anatomic failure rate'

results.measure: Bulge symptom plus stage II-or-greater anterior prolapse at minimum 2 years
results.note: No statistically significant difference among groups.
results.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'The composite failure rate'

results.measure: Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory and Pelvic Floor Impact Questionnaire changes
results.note: Reductions did not differ significantly among groups; sexual-function questionnaire changes also did not differ.
results.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'All groups had a reduction'

harms.label: Graft or mesh erosion
harms.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'Erosion rates'
harms.note: P=0.413. Two mesh erosions required operating-room excision; three were asymptomatic and treated with vaginal estrogen. The porcine erosion healed with vaginal estrogen.

harms.label: Reoperation for recurrent anterior prolapse
harms.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'The composite failure rate'
harms.note: Both anterior-prolapse reoperations occurred in the porcine-graft group.

harms.label: New-onset dyspareunia
harms.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'Among individuals who were sexually active'
harms.note: Seven cases among women sexually active at baseline without dyspareunia; arm-specific denominators were not supplied in the narrative.

harms.label: Bladder or urethral injury and serious adverse events
harms.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'Erosion rates'
harms.note: No intraoperative bladder or urethral injuries and no serious adverse events were reported.

delivery.label: Freehand vaginal paravaginal reinforcement
delivery.value: After bilateral dissection to the ischial spine and arcus tendineus fascia pelvis, three 0-polypropylene sutures per side fixed a trapezoidal Polyform mesh or Pelvicol porcine dermis graft to the arcus without trocar arms; typical graft width was 6–8 cm distally and 12 cm proximally, with 4–6 cm length. The graft was not attached to apical suspension.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Materials and Methods, operative-technique paragraph; Figure 1

delivery.label: Native-tissue repair
delivery.value: Midline plication with interrupted 2-0 polydioxanone followed by epithelial closure with 2-0 polyglactin and vaginal packing.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Materials and Methods, operative-technique paragraph

delivery.label: Concomitant procedures
delivery.value: Hysterectomy in 40%, midurethral sling in 56%, and apical procedure in 67% of all participants; apical suspension was vaginal or laparoscopic when indicated.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Results, first paragraph; Materials and Methods, operative-technique paragraph

delivery.label: Surgeon delivery
delivery.value: Four fellowship-trained female pelvic medicine and reconstructive surgeons supervised or performed procedures at two teaching centers; two surgeons performed most operations and fewer than 4% were done by the other two.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Materials and Methods, first paragraph; Results, first paragraph
